title: A Day That Feels Stuck
description:
For three years, {name} kept to the conventional path.

He divided whatever he earned, sending the portion he could keep into savings and diversified investments. He avoided the big bets. Safe. And slow.

Today {name} saw a post: someone made 100 million won in a single month on crypto. A classmate cleared a year of {name}'s savings in one shot flipping a presale apartment right.

Whenever money came in, {name} divided it in the same order. It was not the wrong road. But some days the numbers on the screen looked like they had stopped moving.

This was the weight of the orthodox path. Boredom. And the doubt — is this really working?

choices.text: Trust the slow road. Slow isn't losing.
choices.result_text: People chasing one big hit also lose it in one. {name} had seen that. Slow isn't losing. Moved the same amount into the same place again.

choices.text: Just once, looked at the risky side
choices.result_text: Just once. Knowing that's exactly how it starts, {name} opened the chart anyway. Heart sped up a little. Better than boredom. That was the scary part.

choices.text: Admitted the weight, and slept early
choices.result_text: Impatience is usually biggest at 3am. {name} turned off the light. Same pace tomorrow. And that's okay — thought it once more before falling asleep.

title: The Chart at 3AM
description:
Three years off the beaten path.

Leverage, day-trading, the seats nobody else takes. The assets swung wildly. Some months doubled. Some months cut in half.

The problem wasn't the money — it was the sleep. Eyes open at 3am. Hand reaches for the phone before the brain does, pulls up the chart. Red and the heart drops; blue and sleep won't come either.

Three years ago this felt like freedom. Now {name} knows — one wrong click can undo everything.

This was the weight of the unorthodox path. Anxiety. And the doubt — is he actually in control of this?

choices.text: This is my way. Stop and you lose.
choices.result_text: Getting this far came from not stopping. {name} chose to believe that. Looked at the chart again. Decided the shaking hands were just the caffeine.

choices.text: Built a safety net. Won't bet it all.
choices.result_text: People who bet everything lose everything. {name} moved a portion somewhere safe. Returns would shrink — but for the first time, slept through the night without waking.

choices.text: Admitted the weight, left the phone in another room
choices.result_text: The chart won't run away. {name} left the phone in the living room and shut the bedroom door. The hand felt empty. Still — fell asleep staring at the ceiling for the first time in a while.

title: A Three-Year Receipt
description:
Out of nowhere, {name} added up the last three years.

Not just the money. The losses had stacked up too, like receipts.

The number of weekend plans turned down. The days a parent's call got cut short. The years a checkup got pushed back. And — the face in the mirror, clearly more worn than three years ago.

Coming this far toward the goal was real. But the road had a price tag, and {name} was only now reading the bill.

choices.text: Knew the cost going in. See it through.
choices.result_text: Nothing's free. {name} knew that starting out. Folded the bill. Stop here and everything paid so far becomes sunk cost.

choices.text: Decided to reclaim one of the things lost
choices.result_text: Can't undo it all, but one was possible. {name} made the call that kept getting pushed back. Or booked the checkup. A small thing. And breathing got a little easier.

choices.text: Stared at the bill a long time. No answer came
choices.result_text: Couldn't tell if it was right or wrong. Only that pretending not to know was no longer an option. That's usually how awareness starts. Uncomfortably.

title: The Bill from Someone You Trusted
description:
By year four, {name} thought he had learned to read people. The man across from him at the pojangmacha was someone he had moved money with more than once, someone whose circumstances he believed he understood.

The man pushed over a thin envelope. The papers asked {name} to cover his share for just one month.

"Just bridge it under your name, hyung."
{name}: "Why does it need my name?"
"Don't you trust me?"

The signature box brought back the blurred name on Father's guarantee PDF. This was no grand fraud and no amount that would ruin him overnight. That made it hurt more. A large betrayal lets you get angry; a hairline crack first makes you doubt your own judgment.

{name} looked from the envelope to the man's face. When a relationship sends a bill, it usually arrives with trust written across the top.

choices.text: Cut them off. A crack never seals back.
choices.result_text: {name} pushed the envelope back and deleted the number. It was not resolve so much as fatigue. Every person he cut off made the world smaller. This time, at least, he had not put his name in someone else's blank.

choices.text: Tried to understand. They must've had reasons.
choices.result_text: He did not sign, but he listened to how the man had reached this point. People rarely set out to become bad. It might have been foolish to keep believing that. Still, understanding someone and guaranteeing them were different acts, and {name} kept that line.

choices.text: Neither hated nor trusted — just kept distance
choices.result_text: He neither cut the man off nor held him close. The envelope went back; the contact stayed. Exactly that much distance. {name} caught himself sorting people by trust rating. He could not tell whether that was adulthood or erosion.

title: The Cost of Two Empty Places
description:
Monday morning, the two places {name} had left empty over the weekend returned as charges. A cancellation fee and the fare required to move again appeared on separate ledger lines. The unanswered contacts kept only their timestamps.

{name} wrote down no excuse. There was time to repair one thing this week: go in person to someone or some office he had missed, set a new time the other side could confirm, or close one window that could no longer be restored.

Business hours kept shrinking while he edited an apology. {name} chose a movement, not a sentence.

description_if_known.arc_y4_three_promises_missed_father&arc_:
Monday morning, Father's appointment and the place {name} had promised another person both turned gray. A hospital rescheduling fee and the fare required to move again appeared on separate ledger lines. The two contact windows kept only their unanswered timestamps.

{name} wrote down no excuse. There was time to repair one thing this week: go in person to someone he had missed, set a new time the other side could confirm, or close one commitment he could no longer keep.

Reception hours kept shrinking while he edited an apology. {name} chose a movement, not a sentence.

Monday morning, Father's appointment had ended in the hospital record, and the deposit for the contract-review seat had become nonrefundable. Both closing times remained on {name}'s phone to the minute.

He did not write that he had been busy. There was time to repair one thing this week: go to a place he had missed, set a new time the other side could confirm, or withdraw from the contract window in writing.

Business hours kept shrinking while he edited an apology. {name} chose a movement, not a sentence.
description_if_known.arc_y4_three_promises_missed_person&arc_:
Monday morning, a photograph of an empty chair arrived from the place {name} should have kept for a person, and the deposit for the contract-review seat became nonrefundable. No one supplied an excuse for him.

{name} marked that he could repair one thing this week: go in person to someone he had missed, set a new time the other side could confirm, or withdraw from the contract window in writing.

Business hours kept shrinking while he edited an apology. {name} chose a movement, not a sentence.

choices.text: Go now to the person or office he missed
choices.result_text:
{name} booked the nearest ticket and checked the address again. No reply promised that he would be received. He still sent his departure and arrival times.

Whether the door opened belonged to the other side. What {name} left this time was a record of moving, and the time he did not turn away from a closed door.

choices.text: Confirm a new time from dates he can actually keep
choices.result_text:
{name} deleted 'any time' and sent the two hours he could truly clear. He locked the slot the other side chose and cleared travel time on both sides of it.

The new appointment did not erase the old one. It did make clear who would be waiting first next time.

choices.text: Withdraw in writing from one window that cannot be restored
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote the missed time and his own name, then said he would not ask for that window again. Even without a reply, the withdrawal time remained on the server.

One opportunity closed. Time opened to repair what remained, though he did not yet know what that time could restore.

title: That Saying About Money
description:
Even after closing the notebook that held one year of figures, {name} could not sleep. A structure he had not understood a year ago was beginning to show itself across the ledger.

That saying — money attracts money. At first it sounded like a comfort the rich made up. But putting it to work himself, it was real. With 1 million won versus 10 million won, the same rate of return came back at a completely different weight.

And he saw the reverse too. Those with nothing just pay interest until it is over. When the starting lines differ, running at the same speed only widens the gap.

That night, {name} learned that hope and anger could begin with the same number.

description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_reasons_named: In the ledger from that first March, similar amounts belonged to a late finish on one line and the meal that got him through the next day on another. Writing down the reasons had made the structure visible first.
description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_totals_only: That first March, he had reconciled the total and stopped there. The figures were exact; only a full year of entries revealed why equal amounts could carry different weight.

choices.text: Understand the system and ride it
choices.result_text: Cursing an unfair world and understanding the system to use it are two different things. {name} chose the latter. Anger he'd keep only as fuel.

choices.text: Ride it, but never forget the starting lines differed
choices.result_text: If he ever climbed up, he didn't want to become someone who forgot the days of just paying interest at the bottom. {name} wrote the vow down somewhere. Because forgetting was a sure thing.

choices.text: Honestly, the anger was bigger
choices.result_text: Why does one person start with 10 million won and another with 1 million won? {name} knew there was no answer and still held the question a long while. Anger was energy too.

title: Doors Are Opened by People
description:
Nine at night. Only folding chairs remained in the common meeting room after a free public briefing. No one had invited {name} personally. Near the exit, strangers checked the schedule and exchanged contact details while the organizer gathered a few blank visitor cards.

{name} held only the public schedule and one card with no name on it. Opportunity clearly moved through people, but no one he met tonight could yet be called an opportunity.

The elevator was about to close. The organizer had shouldered their bag, and the ride home was enough time to finish the file he had postponed. {name} had one move left to make.

choices.text: Tell the three people by the elevator his name first
choices.result_text: {name} held the closing door and introduced himself and his work. Two people shared their contact details; another named the next public session. The earlier train left without him, and the file in his bag remained unfinished.

choices.text: Ask the organizer for the admission rules and costs first
choices.result_text: The organizer wrote down which meetings were public, which were paid, and who chose the attendees. The elevator closed during the explanation. No contacts were gained, but the conditions for entering were now on paper.

choices.text: Return the visitor card and go prepare alone
choices.result_text: {name} returned the blank card and headed for the station. No new contact entered his phone. On the train, however, he finished the last page of the postponed file. Whether tonight's seat would open again remained unknown.

title: My Turn to Call First
description:
The first payment on last month's debt is due tonight. {name} calls the recipient named on the receipt before opening the transfer screen. The other person skips the greeting. "Do I have to ask first again today?"

The promised amount is larger than what he can send. Emptying next week's living-cost account would cover the gap. To the person on the call, the past month is not three lines of figures. It is nights spent leaving the phone faceup, time taken from another promise, and the humiliation of asking first again.

{name} moves his hand away from Send. He can ask what that person postponed and listen, admit the shortage before he is asked, or empty next week's living money, send the promise, and stay until the anger is finished. Repayment begins with who speaks first, not the receipt.

choices.text: Ask what that person had to postpone, then listen to the end
choices.result_text:
"What did you have to put off because of this money?"

The other person gives a short laugh. "You're asking that now. I had someone I needed to call first today. I missed that call waiting for yours." They never say who it was or what they meant to say. {name} offers no defense and listens through the silence that follows.

The first payment goes through only after the date changes. The other person confirms it without saying thank you. "Next time, call before I have to ask." When the screen goes dark, that order remains ahead of the next payment.

choices.text: Say how much he cannot cover before being asked
choices.result_text:
"I can't send all of it tonight. This is what I can send now."

The other person does not ask for the figure again. "You should've said that yesterday. The money being short lasted less than wondering whether you'd disappeared." With no defense left to add, {name} transfers what he can.

The other person chooses the time of the next call. {name} accepts it before checking his own calendar. His ears are still hot after they hang up. If he does not call first next time, money will not be the only thing missing.

choices.text: Empty next week's living money, send the promise, and stay until they hang up
choices.result_text:
{name} empties the account reserved for next week's living costs into the repayment account and makes up the promised amount. Even after the transfer alert sounds, he does not end the call. The other person says nothing for a while. Then the voice comes back low. "The money's here. But if you're going to send a receipt and vanish again, I'll spend another whole day waiting for your call."

{name} says sorry once and waits through every place where the other person stops. By the time the call ends, little sleep remains before his first alarm. The debt is smaller, but food and transit next week face an empty account. Who calls first next time is still unpaid.

title: The Small Print on the Limit Sheet
description:
The preliminary limit estimate was still warm from the printer, and its small type smelled of toner. At 4:40 p.m., {name} read the larger-than-expected number at the top of the bank sheet and the rate changes, income checks, and rejection conditions below it.

The banker highlighted the preliminary maximum. “This estimates what may be approved. It is neither what you can carry nor an official limit.” The monthly payment looked manageable against current income. The box for one month of reduced income was still blank.

Twelve minutes remained. {name} could use them for a risk worksheet, lower his own ceiling and receive an official sheet, or take an official sheet at the preliminary maximum.

choices.text: Add rejection conditions and the payment after an income drop
choices.result_text:
The banker printed a separate risk worksheet with three lines: job loss, reduced income, and a higher rate. The payment beneath the preliminary maximum changed three times.

{name} circled the amount in the worst month. The appointment ended before an official limit sheet could be issued. He left without the large number, but the first point of failure now existed on paper.

choices.text: Recalculate using only what his own current income can repay
choices.result_text:
{name} asked the banker to recalculate from his currently verified income and the amount he could still repay after one reduced-income month. The new limit fell sharply below the first number.

The banker placed both sheets side by side. {name} dated the smaller one. The amount he could be responsible for became clearer than the amount he could obtain.

choices.text: Take the official maximum-limit sheet but do not apply today
choices.result_text:
{name} had an official limit sheet issued at the preliminary maximum and signed only the explanation acknowledgment. He left the application blank. The banker highlighted the sheet's validity date once more.

He left with a document he could use immediately, but without the risk worksheet. No money had entered the account. Only the deadline for deciding again was clear.

title: Across from the Introducer
description:
The unfamiliar introducer's fingernail tapped the empty recipient box twice. At 5:03 p.m. in Sangchul's office, {name}, Sangchul, and the introducer faced one another across a sheet with only the projected return in bold and blanks for the source of the money and the introduction-fee recipient.

Sangchul pushed over a cup of cold instant coffee. “If you write every name first, the good seats are already gone. You enter by judging the person.” The introducer pinned down the corner of the sheet but did not offer a name.

Fifteen minutes remained before the next appointment. Asking about the source, forcing the costs onto paper, or stopping at the blank terms would each leave a different loss.

choices.text: Make both men write their names and identify who supplies the money
choices.result_text:
{name} pointed to the two blank boxes. The introducer produced a card; Sangchul wrote only the funding company's name. The pen stopped when {name} asked for the individual behind it.

The next appointment time passed. The answer was incomplete, but the paper and card now showed exactly who had refused to write a name.

choices.text: Have them itemize the introduction fee and every later charge
choices.result_text:
The introducer first called it ‘customary.’ When {name} pushed over a blank page, the man separated an opening fee, materials, and a success charge. Sangchul stirred the cold coffee.

By the time three cost lines and their billing dates existed, the time to leave for the next address had passed. The cost sheet remained, but the individual funder's name was still blank, and that day's next door had closed.

choices.text: Say there will be no next meeting without written terms
choices.result_text:
{name} left the sheet unfolded at the center of the table. “I won't go to the next address while those boxes are blank.”

The introducer stood first. Sangchul did not stop him. No next address arrived from this meeting. What remained on {name}'s phone was a photograph of the blank boxes and the time the man left.

title: The Name Behind the Card
description:
A temporary site office occupied the second floor of a shopping block marked for demolition. Redevelopment plans covered the walls; zone passes and hard hats lay across folding tables. Before the attendees, Sangchul rested a hand lightly on {name}'s shoulder.

"I brought this man."

The introducer column already read ‘Lim Sangchul’ beside {name}'s name. Nothing stated what the visit would demand later or whether the next seat carried a charge. The site coordinator said the elevator would leave soon with a small group for one zone. Sangchul fanned three passes in one hand.

"Questions come after you get inside."

{name} had to decide whether to demand terms first, narrow the visit, or stop at an unwritten condition.

choices.text: Ask about the introducer and costs in front of everyone
choices.result_text: {name} pointed to the attendance sheet and asked them to write down who introduced whom and which later costs could arise. While the coordinator added two lines, the elevator left. The terms remained on paper; the first site walk did not.

choices.text: Accept one person's pass for one zone only
choices.result_text: {name} chose one coordinator and one zone to inspect. Sangchul collected the other two passes. The broad introduction disappeared, but who he was meeting and where they were going stayed clear to the end.

choices.text: Return the pass unless the terms are written down
choices.result_text:
When Sangchul did not answer, {name} placed the pass back on the table and asked for ‘entry declined because terms were not disclosed’ to be written beside his name. The coordinator added the reason to the visit record and let him photograph that line.

The safety briefing began and the group moved through the inner door. {name} lost the site walk, but kept one record showing that he had not entered under unexplained terms.

title: Under Her Name
description:
At the entrance to a private Gangnam housing briefing, the clerk checked the list twice and could not find {name}. Jiyeon showed the invitation on her phone, and the clerk took out one wristband.

"We can register him as one guest accompanying Han Jiyeon."

The desk screen displayed ‘Han Jiyeon — one guest’ first. Jiyeon did not sign for him. She pushed the pen toward {name}.

"I opened this door, Minjun. You decide what you say inside. Just don't pretend my name was never used to bring you here."

Eight minutes remained before the first session. {name} could reintroduce himself under his own name, ask what Jiyeon's family would expect to hear, or leave the wristband and keep only the conversation between them.

choices.text: Erase the guest label and explain his own name and work
choices.result_text: Before accepting the wristband, {name} asked the clerk to remove the guest label. The first entry line began moving while he explained his name and work from the beginning. The clerk issued a separate waiting number. He missed the first session, but the next-session list carried his own name. Jiyeon waited beside the empty desk without rushing him.

choices.text: Ask what Jiyeon's family would expect before going in
choices.result_text: Jiyeon darkened her screen. "Father doesn't know yet. When he does, he'll ask why you came here, Minjun." They did not rehearse an answer. The first session passed while the wristband stayed on the counter.

choices.text: Decline the wristband and talk with Jiyeon outside
choices.result_text: {name} returned the guest wristband and moved to a bench beyond the lobby. He missed the presentation. When he asked why she had used her name, Jiyeon answered, "I hated rooms filled only with Father's choices. If you came in, at least one person there would be someone I chose."

title: At the Casino Door
description:
At the Jeongseon casino entrance, the shuttle attendant opened the reservation list. Beside {name}'s name was ‘Lim Sangchul's party,’ but Sangchul had gone in ahead and did not answer his phone. The attendant handed over a temporary pass and pointed to a table number inside.

"Your group has already exchanged its cash. They're starting soon."

Beyond the glass, people addressed one another by industry and title. Entering without asking who shared the table could settle the relationship before the money moved. Across the lobby stood the cashier and the lockers. The last shuttle to Seoul would leave in thirty minutes. {name} could not keep the pass, all the cash he brought, and the ride home at once.

choices.text: Ask for the names and relationships at the table before entering
choices.result_text: The attendant reopened the list and identified three people and each connection to Sangchul. During the explanation, one reserved seat went to another guest. {name} remained outside with the pass, while every bill he brought stayed untouched.

choices.text: Keep only the cash he can afford to lose and lock away the rest
choices.result_text: {name} took out only the amount set in advance and locked the wallet and remaining cash away. On the exchange receipt, he wrote the number at which he would stop. The door opened, but the locker key kept its weight in his pocket.

choices.text: Return the pass and take the last shuttle to Seoul
choices.result_text: {name} gave the pass back and crossed to the bus bay. He sent Sangchul one line: "I'm not going in tonight." The cash stayed folded. When the bus door closed, the casino lights began to recede.

title: A Time Already Past
description:
One address remained inside a calendar alert that had faded gray. At 11:43 p.m., its visit time still marked the one place {name} could actually have reached today, but no arrival record carried his name.

The person who sent the address had left one short message: ‘Today's session has ended.’ Beneath it sat the end time and confirmation number for the paid shift {name} had kept instead. One side of the screen held an address he had not reached; the other held work he had actually finished on the same date.

Choosing no door had still spent the day. Now he had to decide how to record the missed promise: apologize directly, keep the address and time as an open record, or keep only the completed shift and close the contact route too.

choices.text: Contact one person and apologize for not going today
choices.result_text: {name} named that place and time and apologized without an excuse. The only reply was, "Today's session has ended." No new date followed. At least one ignored conversation moved from the bottom of the screen to the top.

choices.text: Record the missed address, time, and ‘did not arrive’
choices.result_text: {name} wrote ‘did not arrive’ beside that address and time. A blank that was neither profit nor expense became a record for the first time. No message went out, and the completed-shift confirmation remained on its separate line.

choices.text: Keep only the completed shift and close the missed address and contact thread in the archive
choices.result_text:
{name} attached only the paid-shift confirmation to the ledger. He moved the gray address notice and its conversation into an archive labeled ‘Closed Doors’ and removed them from the first screen.

What he had missed on the day he protected his income survived only in the archive title. This month's record kept neither an address to revisit nor an open thread in which to apologize.

title: The Introduction's Second Bill
description:
Only the coordinator field beside ‘network management’ was blank on the itemized bill. At 11:36 p.m., the payment screen showed last month's redevelopment travel and materials charges; the one zone {name} had actually entered and the other coordinator name on the bill both matched.

Paying in full before midnight would avoid an overdue mark. Calling the coordinator could verify some items, but the deadline might pass while he waited. Removing the unexplained line would cost less and leave an objection on record, along with an open balance.

{name} matched the pass number to the invoice and pressed the transfer amount again. One door had returned as three separate charges.

choices.text: Have the coordinator read each item and pay only the verified charges
choices.result_text:
{name} called the site coordinator and matched the dates for travel and materials one by one. Midnight passed during the explanation of the management fee, but he transferred the two verified amounts.

The bill remained ‘partially paid.’ Beside the call record, two explained lines and one line without a basis stayed visibly separate.

choices.text: Pay in full before the deadline and preserve the original invoice
choices.result_text:
{name} paid all three items and stored the completion screen beside the original invoice. It was eleven minutes before midnight.

No overdue mark appeared. The meaning of ‘network management’ remained blank, however. The payment closed; the question moved behind the receipt.

choices.text: Remove the unexplained fee and send the rest with a written objection
choices.result_text:
{name} paid only travel and materials and wrote, ‘Please identify the service and recipient for the management fee.’ The coordinator read it without replying.

Only the verified amount left the account. One unpaid line remained on the invoice, and {name} captured it together with the written objection.

title: Before the Person Who Waited
description:
The coordinator from last month's site left the new materials closed, a cold paper cup between them. At 9:18 p.m., when {name} sat across from him in the express-bus terminal, their review appointment was already thirty-eight minutes late.

“If you couldn't make the agreed time, did you at least know whose name held the seat?”

On {name}'s phone, Sangchul's address, the time he had read it, and the record of the other work he had actually finished remained separate. Showing everything would explain the delay and hand over another person's name. Naming only his own choice would preserve responsibility and conceal part of the cause. Apologizing without asking for another date would return the power to reopen the relationship to the person who had waited.

choices.text: Show Sangchul's address and the actual times, then explain from the beginning
choices.result_text:
{name} placed the phone on the table and showed Sangchul's address, the time he had seen it, and the order in which the delay happened. The coordinator paused at Sangchul's name.

“Now I know why. I'll decide whether to contact you for another review.” No new date was set. The explanation and the time spent waiting remained beside the cold coffee.

choices.text: Leave out other names and say only what he chose first
choices.result_text:
{name} did not open anyone else's message. “I finished something else first, and I also failed to warn you in time.”

The coordinator asked for no further reason and wrote ‘thirty-eight minutes late’ on the appointment sheet. One name stayed private; an empty part of the explanation stayed too. No new date was offered.

choices.text: Apologize without asking for another date
choices.result_text:
{name} named the late time and the waiting he had caused, then apologized without an excuse. “Whether we meet again should be your decision.”

The coordinator threw away the paper cup and stood. No answer and no new appointment remained. On the terminal bench, only {name} and the original meeting time were left.

title: How Far to Erase the Next Seat
description:
Beneath the seat number Sangchul had sent, one more line read, ‘the same people as last time.’ At 8:50 p.m., the address for the next private dinner and the ten minutes left before the reply deadline shared one screen, while {name}'s calendar already held another repeating invitation at the same hour.

Canceling only tonight would leave the channel open. Asking to be removed from the invitation list could also cut off the next proposal. Refusing every seat until written terms arrived would close the door and leave a reason on record.

No typing indicator appeared in Sangchul's chat. After ‘I can't come,’ {name} had to decide in his own words how much else to close.

choices.text: Cancel only this seat and say he will review future proposals separately
choices.result_text:
{name} named the date and seat number and declined only this invitation. Sangchul replied, “Understood. We'll look at the next one separately.”

A strike appeared through tonight's address. The conversation and the route for another proposal remained open; only one seat had closed.

choices.text: Ask for his name to be removed from the repeating invitation list
choices.result_text:
{name} asked to be removed not only from tonight's seat but from the list that kept bringing the same group together. Sangchul read it at once and did not answer for a long time.

After the deadline, four words arrived: “I'll do that, then.” The address disappeared, and no next date stayed pinned above the conversation.

choices.text: Refuse every seat until the terms arrive in writing
choices.result_text:
{name} asked for the introducer, fees, and attendance terms in writing and said he would not attend tonight or any later seat before receiving them.

Sangchul replied, “You've grown fond of paper.” The address vanished from the calendar, but no document arrived. The reason for canceling and an empty attachment box remained on the same screen.

title: Three Places, One Weekend
description:
Saturday, 3:18 p.m. Three times overlapped on {name}'s phone. At four he had a call with Father's ward to reconcile the medication chart; at four thirty, a review of the deal's source terms; at five, a promise with Daeun outside the convenience store where they first met. Once travel was included, he could keep only one.

Daeun wrote, ‘I'll wait where we first agreed.’ The deal lead would hold the review seat only until 4:40. Father had limited access to the ward phone and would answer once, at four. No one canceled another promise for him.

{name} put all three alerts on one screen and pressed the one he would protect. The other two already carried their closing times.

choices.text: Keep the four o'clock call and reconcile Father's medications
choices.result_text:
{name} called the ward and matched each medication the nurse read against the times in Father's notebook. At the second drug, Father caught his breath. "I missed the evening one." {name} did not switch screens before the call ended.

At 4:40, the deal seat was canceled. Daeun sent one photograph of the convenience store's refrigerator light. One call had been kept, and the timestamps of two empty places were stored with it.

choices.text: Cancel the review and go to where Daeun is waiting
choices.result_text:
{name} told the deal lead he was giving up today's seat and boarded the subway. Daeun waited outside the convenience store with one canned coffee in her hand. "Don't give me the other two cancellations as a debt. Tell me only that you came here today."

{name} turned the other screens facedown and walked with her for an hour. The ward call ended as a missed record, and the review deposit became nonrefundable.

choices.text: Go to the review room and finish the source terms and gap
choices.result_text:
{name} logged his arrival in the review room at 4:27. When the deal lead opened the source terms and financing-gap table, he marked the issuer, recovery date, and added fees in order. The last line was confirmed at 5:12.

The ward phone took no more calls, and Daeun wrote, ‘I'm going home today.’ The document gained a completed-review mark. The time two people had spent waiting entered no attachment.

title: The Right to Correct
description:
Saturday, 2:50 p.m. Three times overlapped beneath the departure board at Seoul Station. At four, {name} had a call with Father's ward to reconcile the medication chart; at four thirty, a contract review in Seoul; at 6:10, a promise to meet Jiyeon at Busan Station. Twelve minutes remained before boarding closed.

Jiyeon wrote, ‘Do not turn this into a story where I came to Seoul. I am waiting in Busan today.’ The deal lead would hold the seat only until 4:40, and the ward could connect once at four.

{name} had to buy the ticket, find a quiet place for the call, or remain in Seoul and go to the review room. Pressing one would make the other two times unrecoverable.

choices.text: Delay boarding and keep the four o'clock call with Father
choices.result_text:
{name} entered a quiet call booth in the station and connected to the ward. The Busan train departed while he matched the nurse's medication names against Father's notebook. Father ended with, "You heard it yourself. That's enough."

The review seat was canceled. Jiyeon received no invented photograph of an empty chair, only {name}'s sentence that he would not arrive. The kept call and two missed times remained on the same screen.

choices.text: Board for Busan and arrive at the time promised to Jiyeon
choices.result_text:
{name} scanned his ticket before boarding closed. From the train, he sent the ward and the deal lead the time he would not arrive. Jiyeon was outside the Busan Station gates, checking her watch.

"Don't make tonight larger by saying you abandoned other promises for it," she said. {name} nodded and put away the phone. What they kept was one evening that began in Busan.

choices.text: Remain in Seoul and review the contract source and gap
choices.result_text:
{name} canceled the Busan ticket and entered the review room at 4:27. He compared the issuer on the source terms with the financing-gap table and obtained one written termination date. The meeting ended at 5:14.

The ward call did not connect again, and Jiyeon returned alone from Busan Station. ‘I will remember the time you chose not to come, not merely the fact that you were in Seoul.’ Her last message remained beneath the negotiation notes.

title: A Witness Through the Speaker
description:
Saturday, 3:18 p.m. No partner's name appeared in {name}'s calendar. Instead, a four o'clock call with Father's ward, a four-thirty review of the source terms, and the 5:10 cutoff for his own after-hours clinic overlapped on one screen. His fingertips had been trembling since morning.

The ward could connect once at four. The deal lead had already charged a seat deposit. The clinic instructions said intake existed only if the patient arrived and showed identification. No one else could enter any of the three windows for him.

{name} did not fill the empty space with an invented lover, friend, or broker. He chose the one place he would actually reach today: Father, his own body, or the deal.

choices.text: Keep the ward call at four and verify Father's medications
choices.result_text:
{name} connected to the ward and read the names and times on each medication packet. Father admitted missing one evening dose, and the nurse recorded the next check. {name} did not open another alert before the call ended.

The deal-seat deposit was lost, and after-hours intake closed. One person's medication had been verified; {name}'s trembling hand and the closed deal window remained.

choices.text: Go to after-hours intake and show someone his own symptoms
choices.result_text:
{name} placed his identification on the intake desk and gave the time the tremor had started. A nurse repeated his blood pressure and sent the symptom record to the night physician. Only after a waiting number appeared did {name} sit down.

The ward call closed, and the deal lead canceled the seat. The only person actually examined today was {name} himself.

choices.text: Go to the review room and verify the source terms and gap
choices.result_text:
{name} reached the review room at 4:27 and marked the issuer, liability end date, and added fees in the source terms. The deal lead pointed first to the guarantor box when he saw that {name} had come alone; {name} said he was confirming figures only.

The ward took no more calls, and clinic intake closed. The document kept a completed-review time. No other person's name appeared in the room.

title: Daeun at Two A.M.
description:
At 2:12 a.m., the bell rang for the third time. When {name} opened the door, Daeun saw his sweat-soaked shirt, shaking hand, and the cup on the floor. She stopped one step short. "Minjun, may I hold your arm? Or should I call emergency services first?"

The laptop showed a client-file deadline of 2:30. After-hours intake was an eleven-minute taxi ride away; eighteen minutes remained to finish the file. He could not do both.

Daeun did not decide for him. {name} had to open the door and seek care, return to the client deadline, or send Daeun away and endure alone.

description_memory_if_known.arc_y4_missed_cost_seen&arc_y4_missed_co: Just before this, {name} had traveled to one of the two places he missed and left departure and arrival times. The door could not be assumed to have opened, but the cost of actually moving followed him into this choice.

Just before this, {name} had offered two workable times and locked the one the other side confirmed into his calendar. The new promise did not erase the old one, and tonight again held only one time he could protect.
Just before this, {name} had withdrawn in writing from one window that could not be restored. The closure freed time, but that time did not solve his body or deadline by itself.

choices.result_text:
"Below the elbow. I'll call the taxi myself." Daeun held only the place {name} allowed and matched his pace into the hall. At intake, {name} gave the onset time and the moment his vision doubled.

At 2:30, the client file closed unsubmitted. Daeun sat outside the exam-room door, and {name}'s name remained on the night intake list.

choices.text: Ask Daeun to leave and finish the client file
choices.result_text:
Holding the handle, {name} said, "I have to send this file. I'll contact you when it is done. Please go now." Daeun sent the clinic address and stood outside until the door closed.

The file was submitted at 2:28. Intake ended, and Daeun's final message gained only a read mark. The tremor continued above the keyboard.

choices.text: Close the door and endure alone without handing it to anyone
choices.result_text:
{name} accepted only the water bottle and closed the door. Daeun said from the hall, "I'll contact you once in ten minutes," but {name} turned the phone facedown.

The client file was not sent, and he did not reach intake. After the corridor light went out, only the refrigerator motor and uneven breathing remained in the room.

title: A Call Open from Busan
description:

"Minjun, set the phone on the floor and give only the onset time. I will not decide for you." His laptop showed a client deadline of 2:30, and after-hours intake in Seoul was an eleven-minute taxi ride away.

From Busan, Jiyeon could remain on the line while he contacted emergency services. In Seoul, {name} could open the door. Or he could return to the deadline, or end the call and remain alone.

The file was submitted at 2:28. Intake passed, and Jiyeon's message received no answer. Only the last call time remained on the black screen between Busan and Seoul.

choices.result_text:
{name} refused location sharing and ended the call. Jiyeon did not call again. She left one line: ‘When you can respond, send a single character.’

The file was not submitted, and {name} did not reach intake. After the Seoul room went dark, one unsent character waited on the Busan screen.

title: The Door Still Shut
description:
At 2:12 a.m., {name} sat on the entryway floor with an after-hours help page open. His fingertips shook, and a tight line ran from his left temple into his neck. The screen held an emergency-call button, a client-file deadline of 2:30, and the final intake time.

No continuing partner or reconnected friend could be assumed to be in the room. Unless {name} spoke, the only other person who could know about his body was a medical dispatcher.

He had to share his location and seek care, submit the deadline file, or contact neither and endure alone.

The laptop showed the client deadline of 2:30 and the final after-hours intake time. Hyunsu could neither call nor open the door for him.

{name} had to share his location and seek care, end the call and submit the file, or hand it to no one and endure alone.

choices.text: Read the address and onset time to emergency services, then unlock the door
choices.result_text:
{name} read the address, onset time, and location of the pain in separate sentences. He kept the call open, unlocked the entryway, and let the corridor light into the room.

The client file closed unsubmitted. The footsteps that entered later belonged not to an unnamed savior, but to medical staff following the dispatch record.

choices.text: Close the help screen and submit the client file by 2:30
choices.result_text:
{name} canceled the assistance screen and returned to the keyboard. The file was submitted at 2:29, and the client server returned an intake time.

After-hours care closed. Even after the completed mark appeared, his fingertips did not stop, and no one verified that fact.

choices.text: Close the call and file, lock the door, and endure alone
choices.result_text:
{name} shut every screen and checked the entryway lock. He lay back against the floor and waited for the shaking to ease.

The client file was not sent, and no medical intake was created. Until morning, the only evidence was the time the work log stopped.

title: A Future at the Same Table
description:
At three on Saturday afternoon, Father's restaurant reservation was for six. Daeun said she could open the door with {name} if she received the address by 5:30. At the same time, a client offered the full overdue fee if {name} worked on-site from five to ten.

{name} could send Daeun the address and enter together, draw a boundary by saying he would go alone, or take the paid assignment and leave the table empty.

Neither Father nor Daeun was described as already seated. The movement and address {name} sent now would determine who actually attended.

choices.text: Send Daeun the address and open the restaurant door together
choices.result_text:
{name} sent the address and reservation name, then waited outside for Daeun. At 6:02, they opened the door side by side. Looking at three bowls, Father asked Daeun, "Will you stay in Seoul to fit Minjun's plan?"

Daeun set down her glass. "I will speak for my own plan, Father." {name} did not answer for her. The paid assignment marked him absent, and the uncomfortable table truly began.

choices.text: Tell Daeun he will go alone and arrive at the family table
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote to Daeun, ‘I will keep this as a place where I answer alone today.’ She did not call that an agreement. She replied, "Do not say you chose it because of me."

{name} entered the restaurant before six and sat across from Father. No name was attached to the empty chair. He missed the paid assignment; only the responsibility to explain why he came alone remained at the table.

choices.text: Cancel the restaurant and go to the paid site at five
choices.result_text:
{name} canceled two places at the restaurant and sent Daeun and Father the same line separately: ‘I am going to the paid site today. I will not pretend the two of you met.’

His site entry was recorded at five, and the fee was paid. No soup was served at the restaurant. Daeun and Father remained people who had never seen each other's expression.

title: Three People's Right to Correct
description:
At 12:40 on Saturday, Father's Seoul restaurant reservation was for six, and the last train that gave Jiyeon comfortable time to travel from Busan left at 1:10. She wrote, "If you confirm by 12:55 that you want me there, I will buy my own ticket." She was not described as already in Seoul.

At the same time, a client offered the overdue fee if {name} worked on-site from five to ten. He could ask Jiyeon to travel and attend together, meet family alone, or go to the paid site.

One choice cost a Busan-Seoul round trip, one left an empty chair, and one spent the entire table.

choices.text: Confirm with Jiyeon and let her book the trip from Busan to Seoul
choices.result_text:
At 12:50, {name} wrote, ‘I want us to go together.’ Jiyeon bought a Busan departure under her own name and shared the seat number. At 6:03, they met outside the restaurant and entered together.

When Father asked whether they would live in Seoul, Jiyeon corrected him first. "I still live in Busan. I made a round trip today." The paid site was lost, but the table and travel cost became real records.

choices.text: Do not ask Jiyeon to travel; go to the family table alone
choices.result_text:
Before 12:55, {name} wrote, ‘I will go alone today.’ Jiyeon replied, "Do not say that I refused," and remained in Busan.

{name} reached the restaurant before six. Instead of explaining why Jiyeon was absent, he named his own decision to come alone. The empty chair did not invent a person in Seoul who had never left Busan.

choices.text: Close the restaurant and travel plan; go to the paid site at five
choices.result_text:
Before Jiyeon bought a ticket, {name} withdrew the travel request and canceled the restaurant. He separately told Jiyeon and Father that he would not speak as if they had met.

His site entry was recorded at five, and the fee was paid. Neither the Busan departure nor the Seoul table opened. What remained was the payment time and a cancellation sent to two people.

title: Soup Set for Two
description:
At three on Saturday afternoon, the family restaurant reservation was for six. This route could assume no partner who might attend. At the same time, a client offered the overdue fee if {name} worked on-site from five to ten.

{name} could arrive alone at the restaurant, confirm a new date with family and go to the site, or take the paid job without creating another promise.

No lover's or friend's name was needed for the empty chair. Only {name}'s movement and sent record would determine attendance or absence.

choices.text: Decline the paid site and arrive alone at the family table
choices.result_text:
{name} declined the site and entered the restaurant before six. The family member looked once at the empty chair and said only, "You came alone."

{name} invented no absent person's circumstances. He stated only that he had chosen to come alone. Two bowls arrived, and the paid fee went to someone else.

choices.text: Confirm next Saturday with family, then go to the paid site
choices.result_text:
{name} did not write ‘next time.’ He sent next Saturday at six, the restaurant, and the reservation name. After the family member confirmed the time, he traveled to the five o'clock site.

Today's table did not open, and the fee was paid. A new promise appeared in the calendar without erasing the place he left empty today.

choices.text: Cancel the table without a new date and go to the paid site
choices.result_text:
{name} told the restaurant and family that he would not come, adding no new date. At five, his name entered the site log.

The fee was paid, and the family table expired. No partner appeared in the empty chair, and no friend was invented as someone who had waited instead.

title: The Table Never Set
description:
At 7:20 on Saturday evening, {name} still had not left for the restaurant. The family reservation closed at eight. His phone held one line: ‘Are you coming today?’ This record contained no partner's name and no soup that had already been served.

A taxi could still get him there alone before the last order. He could call and set a new date the other side confirmed. If he did nothing, both the table and any repair would close.

{name} chose an action for the remaining forty minutes, not a late apology.

choices.text: Take a taxi and arrive alone before the last order
choices.result_text:
{name} sent his expected arrival and got into a taxi. At 7:57, he opened the restaurant door. The family member was waiting at a table with only water.

"You did come." Two bowls arrived late after that. The fare and waiting time remained together. No name was attached to the empty chair.

choices.text: Call now and set a new date and place the other side confirms
choices.result_text:
Before the restaurant closed, {name} called and began by saying he had not come. After a long silence, the family member confirmed next Saturday at six in the same restaurant.

{name} entered the call end time and new reservation number in the calendar. Today's empty table remained; the next one opened as a promise the other side had accepted.

choices.text: Make no contact and let the reservation and repair expire
choices.result_text:
{name} closed the draft and watched eight o'clock pass. The reservation canceled automatically, and no new date appeared.

No one's reaction was invented. After the screen went dark, only the reservation's closing time and one unanswered line remained.

title: The Blank for a Name
description:
A proposed co-obligor agreement lay open in the review room. It named Hangang First Finance as lender, 180 million won as principal, November 30, 2030 as maturity, and the project interest plus {name}'s deposit-return claim as collateral. Daeun's proposed box was empty, and neither signature line held a mark.

After reading early recovery and joint liability, Daeun said, "Time we spent living together does not mean you may borrow my name. Decide whether you want time to review or a person to carry the liability."

{name} could request a smaller revision under his name alone, give Daeun the full copy and ask only whether she wished to review, or withdraw the name request and close today's deal window. None created Daeun's consent or signature in advance.

description_memory_if_known.arc_y4_family_partner_daeun: The earlier family-table record identified Daeun as the person in the relationship route. It did not decide whether she attended that table, and her name and signature still required separate consent here.

choices.text: Delete the co-obligor box and receive a revision under his name
choices.result_text:

Daeun checked the deleted box and put down the pen. "I can see that time we lived together was not converted into contract scale." Another person's name was protected; the larger scale was lost.

choices.text: Give Daeun the full copy and ask only about review in three days
choices.result_text:
{name} gave Daeun the full four-field copy and joint-liability schedule. "In three days I will ask only whether you want to keep reading. I will not ask for a name or signature."

Daeun recorded only the receipt time and returned the pen. The deal seat remained on narrower terms for three days, while their evening became separate time to read the document.

choices.text: Withdraw the request for Daeun's name and close the deal window
choices.result_text:

Daeun watched until the filing screen showed no trace of her name, then stood first. The relationship still carried responsibility; the deal window closed.

title: A Deadline Before the Name

Jiyeon matched page numbers and issue times without touching the blank name box.

"If my name preserves the scale, first say who retains ownership and control," she said. Her travel from Busan did not become a duty to answer today.

{name} could reduce the agreement to his name, guarantee the full copy and independent review time while asking only whether she wished to continue, or withdraw the name request and close the window. No signature or consent existed yet.

description_memory_if_known.arc_y4_family_partner_jiyeon: The earlier family-table record identified Jiyeon in Busan as the person in the relationship route. It did not decide whether she attended the Seoul table, and long-distance travel was not consent to use her name or signature now.

Jiyeon confirmed the receipt time and return method. Today's deal seat narrowed. Her travel and class background did not become consent.

choices.result_text:

Jiyeon read the record and closed her bag. She kept control of her name; {name} lost today's deal window.

title: The Co-Obligor Box Left Blank
description:
The proposal before the deal lead named Hangang First Finance as lender, 180 million won as principal, November 30, 2030 as maturity, and the project interest plus {name}'s deposit-return claim as collateral. The co-obligor box was blank, and no other person's name entered the room.

"One other name restores the scale. It does not have to be a lover," the lead said.

Without using another person's name, {name} could fix a smaller solo scale, file a counteroffer containing his name alone, or withdraw the deal window. Writing someone down as a possibility was not an option.

description_memory_if_known.arc_y4_family_no_partner: The earlier family-table record had no partner who might attend. This co-obligor box could not be filled by inventing a lover or friend later; only terms {name} actually filed under his own name remained.

The scale fell again, but the subject of every condition was fixed as {name}. The other-name box disappeared from the document.

title: A Blank Among the Records
description:
A public terms page, the deal lead's summary, and {name}'s calculation notes lay on the desk. No single source stated lender, principal, maturity, and collateral together. A name box existed while the beginning and end of liability could not be confirmed.

{name} wrote that if any one of the four fields was missing, no other person's name or signature would enter the file. He could formally request complete terms and pause the process, submit reduced conditions under his name alone, or withdraw because the records conflicted.

There was no option to fill the blanks by inference or manufacture another person's consent.

description_memory_if_known.arc_y4_family_no_partner: The earlier family-table record had no partner who might attend. The documentary blanks could not be filled with an invented lover's or friend's name either; all four fields had to come from an official source.

A filing number appeared, but no contract formed. The four unknowns remained unknown.

title: The Night the Bills Arrived
description:
At 11:47 p.m., a 487,300-won bill issued by Changwon Sacred Heart Hospital's billing office would close at 11:59. Seoul East After-Hours Clinic also ended intake at midnight for {name}'s trembling fingers and double vision. Father's ward offered one 11:50 call to reconcile medications, the transfer referral, and the guardian contact chain.

Daeun had come inside after {name}'s message, but she touched no button. "Choose whether to pay, show someone your body, or coordinate Father's ward. Do not turn it into my choice."

Only one action could finish in twelve minutes. Paying a hospital bill was not clinical coordination, and seeking care for himself did not arrange Father's ward.

After-hours intake and the 11:50 coordination call passed. The money arrived, but Father's current medication list, transfer referral, and guardian contact chain were not confirmed. Daeun observed only the payment screen and added no completion.

title: Three Timestamps
description:
At 11:47 p.m., a 487,300-won bill from Changwon Sacred Heart Hospital and Seoul East After-Hours Clinic's midnight intake deadline appeared on one screen. Father's ward offered one 11:50 call to reconcile medications, the transfer referral, and the guardian contact chain.

On a video call from Busan, Jiyeon recorded each issuer and time separately. She was not in {name}'s Seoul entryway and could neither pay nor register for him. "Do not merge money, your body, and Father's ward. Choose the one action you will finish tonight."

{name} had twelve minutes. He did not turn Jiyeon's travel or name into consent.

Seoul intake and the coordination call passed. A payment receipt remained on the Busan screen, but Father's medication, transfer, and guardian links were unconfirmed.

title: One Call and Open Screens

Without handing the decision to an invented person, {name} chose one action for the next twelve minutes.
